prediction.raw: I think you're AITA (As The Adult In The Situation) for not making your 7-year-old brother go to bed. Here's why: While it's understandable that you didn't want to deal with a tantrum and didn't want to be embarrassed, it's your responsibility as the older sibling to set boundaries and ensure your brother gets enough sleep. At 7 years old, children still need a consistent sleep schedule to develop healthy sleep habits and function well during the day. By letting your brother stay up late, you're not teaching him about consequences, as you mentioned. Instead, you're creating a pattern of behavior where he can stay up late and still get away with it. This can lead to long-term sleep problems and other issues. Additionally, your mom trusted you to take care of your brother, and you didn't follow through on that responsibility. While it's not your fault that your friend was getting your brother riled up, it's still your job to make sure your brother gets to bed on time. It's also worth noting that your mom's reaction is not just about being mad at you for letting your brother stay up late. It's also about the fact that you didn't take responsibility for your brother's well-being and didn't follow through on the expectations she had for you. In the future, it's essential to prioritize your brother's sleep needs and set clear boundaries, even if it's inconvenient or difficult. This will help him develop healthy sleep habits and reduce the likelihood of tantrums and other behavioral issues. As for the 2 hours of missed sleep, you're right that it's not a huge deal for a 7-year-old. However, it's still essential to prioritize his sleep needs and ensure he gets enough rest.
